intent: What should I check before installing artificial turf in Shallotte, NC?
distinctValue: Verify property jurisdiction and compare a fully described drainage/access scope instead of assuming a small surface replacement is exempt.

sources.label: Town of Shallotte: Planning & Zoning
supports: The Town describes land-use jurisdiction in town limits and its ETJ, with building-inspection inquiries directed to Brunswick County.

sources.label: Town of Shallotte: jurisdiction and zoning maps
supports: Official maps may lag zoning or annexation changes.

sources.label: Brunswick County Planning & Community Enforcement
supports: "Brunswick County Planning & Community Enforcement provides public planning services for unincorporated areas of Brunswick County that fall outside the planning jurisdictions of municipalities."

sources.label: Brunswick County Stormwater Quality Management and Discharge Control Ordinance (PDF)
supports: Section 1.4 Applicability: "The provisions of the Ordinance shall apply to all areas within the planning jurisdictional limits of Brunswick County."

Section 1.16(b)(ii): "Any activity that disturbs land within 30 feet of the banks of a stream or other natural waterway within the County, except when such disturbance is designated as Exempt or Allowable in the Brunswick County Storm Water Management Manual."

Section 1.16(b)(iii): "Any filling or excavation of a parcel that results in a change of land surface of four (4) inches or more and alters the existing drainage pattern; except instances when said filling or excavation is required for on-site sewage treatment systems that is necessary to meet the requirements of the Brunswick County Department of Health (BCDEH) and that is specifically approved and inspected by BCDEH."
Re-fetched and text-extracted from the PDF directly on 2026-09-13; text matches the quotes already verified for the site's Ash, NC page word for word.

sources.label: Brierwood community site
supports: "Despite it's desirable non-HOA status, community residents take pride in the upkeep and maintenance of their homes."
The community originally featured a golf course that ceased operations in 2017.

sources.label: Brierwood: Government Services
supports: Lists Town of Shallotte Fire Department, Police Department, Parks & Recreation, Planning & Zoning, and Code Enforcement as serving the community.
"Water is billed to Brunswick County and Sewer billed to the town of Shallotte."

supports: Only result returned is Civietown Road Southwest (SR 1132), Fulford, Brunswick County, ZIP 28462, at 33.9794783 / -78.3197121 — no place node exists for a settlement named Civietown.

sources.label: HomeTownLocator: "Sivey Town", Brunswick County, NC
supports: Lists "Sivey Town" as a populated place in Lockwoods Folly Township on the USGS Holden Beach quadrangle, roughly 33.97/-78.31, a likely variant spelling of the same settlement, with Shallotte given as about 4.4 miles away.

claimEvidence.claim: The Town describes land-use jurisdiction in town limits and its ETJ, with building-inspection inquiries directed to Brunswick County.
claimEvidence.source_locator: Planning & Zoning body, jurisdiction and building inspection paragraphs.
claimEvidence.limits: No parcel was geocoded. Mailing-address caution is an inference from the jurisdiction/map distinction, not a determination for any address.
claimEvidence.mappedClaim: Confirm the parcel jurisdiction with Town Planning & Zoning; the mailing address alone does not determine it.

claimEvidence.claim: Civietown has no incorporated town government of its own and doesn't appear as a place on federal or OpenStreetMap place records.
claimEvidence.source_locator: Nominatim search result set for the query "Civietown".
claimEvidence.limits: Confirms no OSM place node and no municipal government; does not itself establish which side of Shallotte's ETJ line any specific parcel falls on — that is stated as unverified on the page.
claimEvidence.mappedClaim: Civietown sits along Civietown Road SW (SR 1132), about 3.8 miles east of Shallotte, and has no incorporated town government of its own.

claimEvidence.claim: Where the county reviews the work, Brunswick County's stormwater ordinance requires a permit for a four-inch-plus grading change that alters drainage, or for disturbance within 30 feet of a stream bank not listed as exempt.
claimEvidence.source_locator: Section 1.16(b)(ii) and 1.16(b)(iii) of the ordinance PDF.
claimEvidence.limits: States the ordinance's general trigger; does not determine whether any specific Civietown parcel is inside the county's jurisdiction versus Shallotte's ETJ, or whether a given dig meets the exemption list in the county's management manual.
claimEvidence.mappedClaim: Filling or excavating a parcel by four inches or more, in a way that changes how it drains, needs a Stormwater Management Plan and a county Stormwater Permit, and any digging within 30 feet of a stream bank needs one too unless the county's management manual marks the work exempt.

claimEvidence.claim: Brierwood has non-HOA status and is served by Town of Shallotte Planning & Zoning and Code Enforcement, with sewer billed by the town and water by Brunswick County; the community's former golf course closed in 2017.
claimEvidence.source_locator: Brierwood community-details page (HOA status, golf course history) and Government Services page (department list, utility billing).
claimEvidence.limits: Confirms the community's own claim of non-HOA status and which departments it names as serving it; does not verify Brierwood's parcel boundary against the Town's ETJ map.
claimEvidence.mappedClaim: Brierwood is a former golf-course community with non-HOA status, served by Town of Shallotte Planning & Zoning and Code Enforcement.
